problem: Existing VLN simulators model motion via kinematic teleportation or treat humanoids as one interchangeable robot type sharing one control proxy. Scene suites are not curated for navigability, and instruction data is rendered under idealized stable-camera conditions with hallucination-prone VLM annotation.
motivation: Bipedal humanoids differ widely in height, DoF and gait, so locomotion dynamics, camera shake and fall risk directly affect VLN success. A benchmark must therefore execute VLN policies under real physics on multiple morphologies, with large traversable scenes and grounded instructions.
key_idea: Build an Isaac Sim benchmark for VLN across four humanoid embodiments, using an RL locomotion policy plus PD/MPC path tracker, navigability-curated Real2Sim (3DGS) scenes, and multi-agent generator-reviewer-paraphraser instruction annotation with human verification.
insight: Embodiment matters a lot under physical execution. The tallest robot (Unitree H1) gives the lowest average SR (20.84% vs 32-37% for the others) and fall rates up to 71% for NaVILA, so SR alone hides stability differences. Model rankings also shift across robots and metrics: JanusVLN is best on average, DualVLN has the lowest mean fall rate, and Internal-A leads SR while G1 leads SPL. A 20-episode sim-real pilot (r=0.935 NE correlation) suggests the reconstructed scenes preserve navigation difficulty, but it is small-scale.
method: Hierarchical control: a per-embodiment RL locomotion policy outputs joint torques; a PD tracker (discrete-action models) or MPC tracker (continuous-action models) converts navigation plans into velocity/heading references.

Plug-and-play interface: the VLN model receives head-camera RGB plus the instruction and emits actions; new models need only this interface, and new robots need a URDF/USD plus a locomotion policy. NaVILA, StreamVLN, DualVLN and JanusVLN are integrated.
Navigability-curated scenes: 87 scenes with verified traversable area >100 m^2 (median 266, mean 387), 17 indoor classes, 6 domains, from artist-designed and 3DGS sources.
3DGS Real2Sim pipeline: gsplat with unbiased depth and depth-normal consistency, TSDF-fused collision meshes packed with the Gaussians in a USDZ, COLMAP-to-Isaac axis transform.

Physics-aware episode sampling: slice the collision mesh at body height into a 2D occupancy map, dilate by the largest robot's footprint, sample start-goal pairs with A*, execute under the full control stack and resample unstable paths.

Multi-Agent Annotation: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B grounds the goal; Gemma-4-31B and InternVL3.5-38B independently build route graphs; reconciliation plus a Qwen3-VL reviewer with deterministic geometric checks; GPT-5.5 paraphrases into Formal/Natural/Casual variants, re-parsed for consistency.
Human-in-the-loop and Fall Rate: 3 annotators review all episodes (20% double-reviewed); a Fall Rate metric uses height-drop/speed criteria T1-T3.

setting.backbone: NaVILA, StreamVLN, DualVLN, JanusVLN (public checkpoints, frozen, zero-shot) on a per-embodiment RL locomotion policy with PD/MPC trackers
setting.training_data: none (benchmark used only for zero-shot evaluation; no models trained or fine-tuned on it)
setting.observation: egocentric head-camera RGB (recorded RGB/depth/IMU with locomotion-induced camera shake)
setting.action_space: discrete forward/turn-left/turn-right/stop with PD tracker (NaVILA, StreamVLN, JanusVLN); continuous velocity with MPC tracker (DualVLN); RL locomotion below
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT geometry priors only used for annotation)

numbers.eval_set_note: all 933 episodes, one instruction per episode, single evaluation set
numbers.extra: PD tracker, physics execution, SR success radius 3.0 m

numbers_note: Table 2 has 16 model-robot rows; only JanusVLN (all four robots) and DualVLN-G1 are partly listed. Robot-averaged SRs: JanusVLN 43.55, StreamVLN 23.63; nDTW: JanusVLN 48.38, DualVLN 43.39, StreamVLN 36.67. Sim-real pilot (DualVLN, G1, 20 episodes): NE Pearson r=0.935, Spearman 0.911, mean abs NE diff 0.68 m, nDTW 78.2±18.8.
results: JanusVLN is best overall (mean SR 43.55, nDTW 48.38), ahead of DualVLN, NaVILA and StreamVLN. Unitree H1 is hardest (mean SR 20.84; fall rate 64.5% for StreamVLN and 71.0% for NaVILA), and DualVLN has the lowest mean fall rate. A 20-episode sim-real pilot shows NE correlation r=0.935.
limitations: Limited scene diversity, human verification as a scaling bottleneck, and high computational cost of full physics simulation.
Sim-real study is a pilot: two scenes, one checkpoint (DualVLN), 20 episodes; 3DGS reconstruction quality is only shown qualitatively.
Only zero-shot evaluation with no fine-tuning; cannot separate morphology effects from locomotion policy/controller differences, and two robots are internal and undisclosed.
